Interim order directed:
Interim suspension order (18 months)

Page 2 of 2
Decision and reasons on interim order

The panel decided to make an interim suspension order for a period of 18 months.

Unless Mr Mani’s case has already been concluded or there has been a material change
of circumstances, a panel will review the interim suspension order at a review meeting
within the next six months and every six months thereafter. A panel will be invited by the
NMC to confirm the interim suspension order at this meeting and Mr Mani will be notified of
the panel’s decision in writing following that meeting.

Where there has been a material change of circumstances that might mean that the order
should be revoked or replaced, or there has been a request for an early review, a panel
will review the interim order at a hearing which Mr Mani will be invited to attend in person,
send a representative on Mr Mani’s behalf or submit written representations for the panel
to consider. At any such review hearing the panel may revoke the interim order, it may
confirm the interim suspension order or it may replace it with an interim conditions of
practice order.

The NMC Case Examiners are yet to decide whether there is a case to answer in relation
to the allegations made against Mr Mani. The NMC will write to Mr Mani when the case is
ready for the next stage of the fitness to practise process.

This will be confirmed to Mr Mani in writing.

That concludes this determination.
